Subject: TenX Hosted Commit: Rollout schedule, throttle migration & onboarding checklist

Hi Samir / Olivia,

Great to see TenX's usage continuing to grow — congrats on the traction. Per our renewal conversation, this thread is to lock down the onboarding/rollout plan for the new hosted monthly commit (upgrade from 2.5M to 5M tokens/month), the related rate-tier changes, and the throttle migration window so Prod traffic doesn't see surprises.

High-level ask: confirm the dates below and any additional approvals you need from procurement/security so we can issue the amendment and schedule the Dedicated onboarding sessions.

Proposed timeline (please confirm):
- Week of Jun 21: Sign amendment (DocuSign link will be circulated)
- Jun 28–Jul 2: Config changes in routing and rate-limits; non-prod validation windows (low risk)
- Jul 5: Production throttle migration (2am–5am PT maintenance window)
- Jul 6–20: Post-migration monitoring and tuning; CS-led usage review

Attachments Im sharing now: TenX_MutualActionPlan_v3.xlsx (detailed checklist), current Throughput_Metrics_June.csv for baseline. Karthik, copied you to add the technical steps and any caveats for prefix caching.

Please reply with any conflicts on dates or approvals needed. If procurement wants a different signature flow, loop them in and well adapt.

Thanks,
Dylan

1) Procurement needs the finalized amendment and a high-level SLA excerpt. Can you send the DocuSign and a one-page SLA snippet?

Olivia and I will loop in Procurement once we have the DocuSign URL and SLA excerpt.

Samir — Jul 6 02:00–05:00 PT works for us, well plan for that. Quick technical notes so your infra team can prepare: 

- Burst cushion: we can enable a 20% temporary burst for the first 30 days tied to the new commit. Its a soft cushion (no SLA guarantee) intended for ramp protection. We can extend if needed but will need a quick follow-up commit amendment if that becomes permanent.
- Prefix/KV cache: During migration we recommend a 45-minute warmup window where non-critical prefixes are pre-warmed from a replay of recent requests. This minimizes cold-starts for common routes.
- Rate tiers: Well map your endpoints to the new tier (5M commit) and apply route-level hard-throttles at 1.6x sustained capacity to preserve latency SLOs. Ops will publish the pre- and post- limits in the shared checklist.

I've attached a quick export of the expected token consumption pattern (Throughput_Metrics_June.csv) so you can cross-check. Laura — can you own the post-migration audit and the first-week quality checks with their SREs?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Following up with the DocuSign and pricing amendment details:

- DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/tenx/commit-amendment (expires in 14 days)
- Amendment: upgrade from 2.5M tokens/month to 5M tokens/month; monthly committed spend tier adjusted accordingly.
- One-page SLA excerpt: Our standard Hosted SLA (99.95% uptime for inference endpoints) is included in the DocuSign packet under Exhibit A.
- Billing: for the first billing cycle under the new commit we will include a one-time credit to offset switching costs (applied after sign). Finance (Mina) is looped for final invoicing flow.

Next steps: please sign the DocuSign by Jun 21 to hit the proposed timeline. If procurement needs PO-first flow we can accommodate — procurement, please advise preferred signing sequence.

Cheers,
